name: Praia (Beachfront Lower Town)
tagline: The flat, walkable heart by the sand
description: The lively lower town spread along Nazare's long beach, packed with restaurants, cafes, guesthouses, and the seafront esplanade. Flat and compact, it is the natural base for most visitors and nomads, with everything walkable and the sand steps from your door.
pros: Right on the main town beach
Best choice of restaurants and cafes
cons: Crowded and pricier in peak summer
Can feel quiet and shuttered in winter

name: Sitio
tagline: Clifftop quarter of viewpoints and legend
description: The historic quarter perched atop the escarpment, reached by the Ascensor da Nazare funicular. Home to the Nossa Senhora da Nazare sanctuary, sweeping viewpoints, and the lighthouse fort overlooking Praia do Norte, it blends pilgrimage tradition with the world's most famous big-wave panorama.
pros: Overlooks the famous Praia do Norte waves

name: Pederneira
tagline: The quiet old hilltop original town
description: Nazare's oldest quarter, sitting on a hill inland from the beach, once the historic core before the town spread to the shore. Sleepy, residential, and largely untouristed, it offers old streets, a viewpoint over the bay, and a calmer, more local pace of life.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads wanting quiet and local life
cons: Uphill and away from the beach
Few shops, cafes, or services nearby

name: Praia do Norte / Porto de Abrigo
tagline: Home of the giant waves and the harbour
description: The north-facing surf coast beyond the Sitio headland, where the deep Nazare Canyon drives record-breaking winter swells at Praia do Norte, plus the sheltered Porto de Abrigo harbour. This is surf-legend territory rather than a residential hub, drawing wave-watchers and tow-surf crews.
cons: Exposed and quiet outside surf season
